evidence.quote: Death rates from a variety of causes have been found to be higher in people with elevated blood lead levels ; these include cancer , stroke , and heart disease , and general death rates from all causes .
Evidence also suggests that age - related mental decline and psychiatric symptoms are correlated with lead exposure .
Some health effects , such as high blood pressure , are only significant risks when lead exposure is prolonged ( over about one year ) .
The toxic effect of lead causes nephropathy and may cause Fanconi syndrome , in which the proximal tubular function of the kidney is impaired .
Lead poisoning inhibits excretion of the waste product urate and causes a predisposition for gout , in which urate builds up . This condition is known as saturnine gout .
